governance.timelockMinDelayNote: 3600 = 1 hour, at launch. 🔴 THIS IS ALSO THE UNPAUSE LATENCY and a brand-new DEX carrying partner flow cannot be down for a day: pausePoolManager is role-or-owner so a monitoring key can stop swaps in seconds, but unpausePoolManager is onlyOwner and the owner is this timelock - so the delay is the floor on recovery from a pause, accidental or hostile. ⚠️ What the shorter delay costs, and it is the reason 86400 was chosen first on 2026-09-07: the delay is the window in which a hostile or mistaken proposal can be spotted and cancelled. See timelockTargetDelay for the raise to 24h that follows once the DEX is settled, and safeSignersNote for why the per-owner CANCELLER grants stopped being optional in the same decision - with only three keys, two of them one person's, an hour only helps if somebody other than the proposer can actually cancel. 🔑 Script 08 checks the LIVE getMinDelay() equals this number on every run, and enforces a one-hour floor on mainnet. The floor used to be 24 hours while this file said 3600, so the one script meant to fail loudly would have failed on a correct deploy - fixed in the 2026-09-08 audit pass (G-2). ✅ What makes both directions survivable: a pause blocks swap and donate ONLY. modifyLiquidity is not paused, so users can always withdraw liquidity while paused.
governance.timelockTargetDelayNote: The delay this deployment intends to RAISE to once the DEX is settled - 86400 = 24 hours. It is recorded rather than left as an intention because the raise is easy to keep postponing and nothing else would ever mention it: script 08 prints it as a standing note for as long as timelockMinDelay is below it. 🔑 HOW THE RAISE IS DONE: `TimelockController.updateDelay` is `onlySelf`, so it is not a call anybody makes - it is an operation the timelock schedules against ITSELF. Safe -> timelock.schedule(timelock, 0, updateDelay(86400), 0, 0, <current delay>), wait, execute. 🔴 And it is TWO changes, not one: script 08 checks the live getMinDelay() EQUALS timelockMinDelay in this file, and ForkLink.t.sol pins that number, so the same PR that executes the raise must move timelockMinDelay to 86400 here. governance.pauserNote: ⚠️ NULL, and that means NOBODY CAN PAUSE without the full timelock delay. `pausePoolManager` on both PoolManagerOwner contracts is role-or-owner, so a monitoring key holding the pause role stops swaps in seconds; `grantPausableRole` is onlyOwner and the owner is the timelock, so granting it is a scheduled operation somebody has to remember - it does not happen as part of any deploy script. choice.treasuryNote: ⛔ NULL, and script 02 reverts on it - readAddress refuses a null - so this must be filled BETWEEN script 01 and script 02. It cannot be pre-filled because it IS the Safe, and the Safe's address is not known until script 01 has created it. ⇒ After script 01, copy governance.safe into this field. That is what testnet does (choice.treasury == governance.safe 0x0ee0Db41...), and it is right for the same reason: protocol revenue should land somewhere the signers already control rather than at a fresh address nobody has tested a withdrawal from. ☑ CONFIRMED 2026-09-08 after the alternative was examined and REJECTED. Choice v1's Treasury Multisig inj1c2yleauy9say73tsx3dk5tvlgwwzdh96r76zv4 was proposed and ruled out on two independent grounds, both read off the chain that day. (1) It has NEVER ACTED: zero proposals created in its lifetime, one of its two voters has no account on chain at all and the other has never sent a transaction on either side. (2) 🔴 THE ONE THAT BITES EVEN IF THAT WERE FIXED: it is a cw3 CosmWasm contract with ZERO EVM code, and `harvest` pays the treasury with an ERC20 `transfer`. For a PURE EVM ERC20 - and mainnet USDC 0xa00C59fF... is exactly that - the balance lands in EVM state at an address whose only occupant is a CosmWasm contract, and a CosmWasm contract cannot make EVM calls. Those tokens would be unreachable by anybody, for ever, no matter who holds the voter keys. Only bank-backed denoms like wINJ would even be theoretically recoverable. A Safe is an EVM contract and has neither problem. 🔑 A PREVIOUS VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID getting the treasury wrong means "a Tier-1 redeploy of both rather than a setting change". THAT IS WRONG and it mattered, because it made this decision look irreversible: `ChoiceFeeController.setTreasury` is `onlyOwner`, so the timelock can move it at any time. It is a constructor argument only in the sense that it must be SET at construction. ✅ Low stakes at launch on top of that: with protocolFeeSplitRatio at 0 nothing is ever collected, so this address receives nothing until the fee is turned on.
choice.protocolFeePolicyNote: 🔴 MAINNET LAUNCHES WITH CHOICE'S PROTOCOL FEE FULLY OFF. Decided 2026-09-08: partners route volume against their own liquidity at no protocol cost, so the only fee a pool charges is its LP leg, which a partner who IS the LP earns straight back. Both numbers are CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENTS to ChoiceFeeController (script 02 reads them from here), not post-deploy calls - under CREATE3 the controller is born owned by the factory's one-shot proxy child with the timelock only as pendingOwner, so between deployment and acceptOwnership there is nobody who could make the call, and pool creation is permissionless, so any pool opened in that window would bake in the wrong policy permanently for that pool. ⚠️ TWO numbers, not one, and the second is the one that gets missed: a DYNAMIC-fee pool never consults protocolFeeSplitRatio at all - upstream's protocolFeeForPool branches on the dynamic flag first and answers defaultProtocolFeeForDynamicFeePool, which ships at 300 (0.03%) - so zeroing only the ratio leaves a live protocol fee on every dynamic-fee pool anybody opens, silently. test/ProtocolFeesDisabled.t.sol pins both. 🔑 TURNING IT ON LATER NEEDS NO REDEPLOY, but it is two different operations: setProtocolFeeSplitRatio(330000) from the timelock restores the plan §4 tier table for pools opened AFTERWARDS, while pools that ALREADY EXIST keep the zero they were born with - a pool's protocol fee is fetched from the controller once, at initialize, and stored - so each one needs its own clFeeController.setProtocolFee(key, fee). Batch those into a single timelock operation. Note testnet deliberately runs the opposite policy (330000/300) so the fee path stays exercised and the frontend's tier table keeps being checked against a live pool.

addressAliases.choice.treasury: the Safe, deliberately - protocol revenue lands where the signers can move it without waiting out a timelock delay. Declared here because the well-formed check treats one address under two keys as a copy-paste until a human says otherwise, and this is the one place it is intended. Testnet declares the same alias for the same reason. See choice.treasuryNote for why Choice v1's cw3 treasury multisig was rejected: it has no EVM code, so a pure EVM ERC20 sent there would be unreachable by anyone for ever.

meta.vaultDeployBlockNote: THE INDEXER'S START BLOCK. The Vault 0xB67dd13b... was created in block 182158111 by tx 0xb11a02cf3dc4771690a625107844147da6d46ac229d1452823520b13186b91d8, and it is the first Choice v2 contract on 1776 that any event can precede - so backend FIREHOSE_START_BLOCK is this number. Too LATE silently skips pools and looks exactly like a quiet chain; too early only costs backfill. 🔴 IT CANNOT BE FOUND WITH backend/scripts/find-deploy-block.sh ON MAINNET, and that is worth knowing before someone spends an hour on it: that script binary-searches eth_getCode, and the endpoints available here prune STATE - the public sentry errors on state a few thousand blocks old, and an ordinary pruned full node keeps far less than the distance back to this block - so eth_getCode at the deploy block answers an ERROR rather than code-or-empty. The script classifies that third state and refuses to guess, by design, so it never converges here. 🔑 What answered instead: the Blockscout internal-transaction trace of the deployer EOA's transactions, which shows create2 -> the one-shot CREATE3 proxy 0x82307E70... and then create -> this Vault, in that transaction. Block DATA is not pruned the way state is - the sentry serves eth_getBlockByNumber and eth_getBlockReceipts at this height (measured 2026-09-08, 1 tx / 1 receipt / 3 logs), which is the property the poller actually depends on.

broadcastDiscipline: ⛔ Never --slow: forge waits for a receipt and strands a multi-tx script after tx 1.

⛔ Never --resume: Injective answers eth_getTransactionReceipt with null for a tx it has already mined, so a broadcast routinely reports failure after the work landed. Confirm with eth_getCode and re-run the script from the top - every script is idempotent for exactly this reason.
🔴 eth_estimateGas UNDER-REPORTS on Injective. Pass an explicit, generous --gas-limit on every write.

🔴 A forge script cannot touch wINJ or any bank ERC20: precompile 0x64 has no code in REVM, so simulation dies and --skip-simulation does not save it. Make the script a calldata printer and send with cast send.
✅ But `cast call --from <admin>` DOES execute on the node, so every admin step can be dry-run for free. Do it.
